flags.name: --help
flags.description: show this help message and exit

flags.name: --custom_tls_config
flags.description: Path to a JSON file containing a specific TLS configuration to check the server against, following Mozilla's format. Cannot be used with --mozilla_config.

flags.name: --mozilla_config
flags.description: Shortcut to queue various scan commands needed to check the server's TLS configurations against one of Mozilla's recommended TLS configurations. Set to "intermediate" by default. Use "disable" to disable this check.

flags.name: --update_trust_stores
flags.description: Update the default trust stores used by SSLyze. The latest stores will be downloaded from https://github.c om/nabla-c0d3/trust_stores_observatory. This option is meant to be used separately, and will silence any other command line option supplied to SSLyze.

flags.name: --cert
flags.description: Client certificate chain filename. The certificates must be in PEM format and must be sorted starting with the subject's client certificate, followed by intermediate CA certificates if applicable.

flags.name: --key
flags.description: Client private key filename.

flags.name: --keyform
flags.description: Client private key format. DER or PEM (default).

flags.name: --pass
flags.description: Client private key passphrase.

flags.name: --json_out
flags.description: Write the scan results as a JSON document to the file JSON_FILE. If JSON_FILE is set to '-', the JSON output will instead be printed to stdout. The resulting JSON file is a serialized version of the ScanResult objects described in SSLyze's Python API: the nodes and attributes will be the same. See https://nabla- c0d3.github.io/sslyze/documentation/available-scan- commands.html for more details.

flags.name: --targets_in
flags.description: Read the list of targets to scan from the file TARGET_FILE. It should contain one host:port per line.

flags.name: --quiet
flags.description: Do not output anything to stdout; useful when using --json_out.

flags.name: --slow_connection
flags.description: Greatly reduce the number of concurrent connections initiated by SSLyze. This will make the scans slower but more reliable if the connection between your host and the server is slow, or if the server cannot handle many concurrent connections. Enable this option if you are getting a lot of timeouts or errors.

flags.name: --https_tunnel
flags.description: Tunnel all traffic to the target server(s) through an HTTP CONNECT proxy. HTTP_TUNNEL should be the proxy's URL: 'http://USER:PW@HOST:PORT/'. For proxies requiring authentication, only Basic Authentication is supported.

flags.name: --starttls
flags.description: Perform a StartTLS handshake when connecting to the target server(s). StartTLS should be one of: auto, smtp, xmpp, xmpp_server, pop3, imap, ftp, ldap, rdp, postgres. The 'auto' option will cause SSLyze to deduce the protocol (ftp, imap, etc.) from the supplied port number, for each target server.

flags.name: --xmpp_to
flags.description: Optional setting for STARTTLS XMPP. XMPP_TO should be the hostname to be put in the 'to' attribute of the XMPP stream. Default is the server's hostname.

flags.name: --sni
flags.description: Use Server Name Indication to specify the hostname to connect to. Will only affect TLS 1.0+ connections.

flags.name: --robot
flags.description: Test a server for the ROBOT vulnerability.

flags.name: --certinfo
flags.description: Retrieve and analyze a server's certificate(s) to verify its validity.

flags.name: --certinfo_ca_file
flags.description: To be used with --certinfo. Path to a file containing root certificates in PEM format that will be used to verify the validity of the server's certificate.

flags.name: --sslv2
flags.description: Test a server for SSL 2.0 support.

flags.name: --sslv3
flags.description: Test a server for SSL 3.0 support.

flags.name: --compression
flags.description: Test a server for TLS compression support, which can be leveraged to perform a CRIME attack.

flags.name: --http_headers
flags.description: Test a server for the presence of security-related HTTP headers.

flags.name: --elliptic_curves
flags.description: Test a server for supported elliptic curves.

flags.name: --tlsv1
flags.description: Test a server for TLS 1.0 support.

flags.name: --reneg
flags.description: Test a server for insecure TLS renegotiation and client-initiated renegotiation.

flags.name: --early_data
flags.description: Test a server for TLS 1.3 early data support.

flags.name: --fallback
flags.description: Test a server for the TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV mechanism to prevent downgrade attacks.

flags.name: --ems
flags.description: Test a server for TLS Extended Master Secret extension support.

flags.name: --tlsv1_1
flags.description: Test a server for TLS 1.1 support.

flags.name: --heartbleed
flags.description: Test a server for the OpenSSL Heartbleed vulnerability.

flags.name: --resum
flags.description: Test a server for TLS 1.2 session resumption support using session IDs and TLS tickets.

flags.name: --resum_attempts
flags.description: To be used with --resum. Number of session resumptions (both with Session IDs and TLS Tickets) that SSLyze should attempt. The default value is 5, but a higher value such as 100 can be used to get a more accurate measure of how often session resumption succeeds or fails with the server.

flags.name: --tlsv1_2
flags.description: Test a server for TLS 1.2 support.

flags.name: --tlsv1_3
flags.description: Test a server for TLS 1.3 support.

flags.name: --openssl_ccs
flags.description: Test a server for the OpenSSL CCS Injection vulnerability (CVE-2014-0224).
